main_text.p: Violatio alicujus] Violatio templi, Liv. Profanum, Plin. i. e. Profanatio.
Violatio pudicitiæ] Violatio pudoris fœminæ. Rupta virginitas, Quint. Vitiatio, Sen. Devirginatio, Scribon. Compressus, us, Plaut. Ludibrium, Curt.
Violator] Violator juris. Ruptor fœderis, Liv. Temerator, Amm.
Violenter] Violentius, Vlp. Vi ac necessitate coactus, Cic. Vi subigente, Lucr. Per vim actum. Per potestatem auferre aliquid alicui, Pro potestate agere, Cic. Per oppressionem eripere, Ter.
Violentia] Vis: vim & manus alicui inferre, Cic. Oppressio, Ter.
Violentus] Violentissima tempestas, Cic. Impetuosus, Plin. Imperiosus. Urgens malum. Fatalis ac necessarius casus, Cic.
Vipera] Excetra. Aspis, Cic. Prester. Cerastes, (i. e. Serpens cornutus,) Plin. Echidna, Ovid.
Vir es] Virum te judico. Macte, Cic. Laudo, Ter. Nolster esto, dum te poteris defensare injuria, Plaut. Tanto major! Tanto augustior! Plin. Iun. Euge & belle, Pers. Vid. Euge.

Virens] Viridis, Cic. Viridans, Virg. Præviridans, Macrob. Perviridis; herbidus color, Plin. Herbeus oculus, Plaut. Vivus cespes, Hor. Vivax gramen, Ovid. Viridicatus, Cic. Porraceus, Plin. Galbus color, Turneb. Prasinus, Bayf.
Vivere] Virescere, Col. Viridantur ab undis grana, Ovid. Viridari ab herbis, Grati. Evirescere, Var. Intervirere, Claud. Vernant agri, Mart. Herbescere, Cic. Viriditatem alicujus imitari, Plin.
Virga ] Flagrum, Liv. Flagellum, Var. Ferula, Iuv. Plin.

page.notes: Catchword "Virge-" is set at lower right, in the printed position. Some words in the left-hand entries are faint; readings such as "Vir es" and "Vivere" follow the print as seen.
